title: Safe Anytime Valid Inference for Linear Models
text: Methodology: - Lindon, M., Ham, D. W., Tingley, M., Bojinov, . (2026). Anytime-Valid Inference Linear Models Applications Regression-Adjusted Causal Inference. Journal American Statistical Association. doi:10.1080/01621459.2026.2692052 (preprint: arXiv:2210.08589). - Lindon, M. (2026). Anytime-Valid Inference Linear Models Clustered Outcomes: Exact Multivariate Tests Cluster-Robust Confidence Sequences. arXiv:2610.25613. Cluster-robust inference via av(fit, cluster = ~ id). title: Safe Anytime Valid Inference for Linear Models
code: devtools::install_github("michaellindon/avlm")  # Generate Data set.seed(1) n = 100 X = scale(replicate(3, rnorm(n)), center = TRUE, scale = FALSE) trt = sample(c(0, 1), size = n, replace = TRUE) y = 1 + 0*X[,1] + 0*X[,2] + 1.4*X[,3] + 2.3*trt + 2*X[,1]*trt + 3*X[,2]*trt + 0*X[,3]*trt + 1*rnorm(n) df = data.frame(X) df$trt = trt df$y = y  # Tune g to minimize the width of the confidence interval at n alpha = 0.05 number_of_coefficients = ncol(model.matrix(y ~ . + trt * ., data = df)) g_star = optimal_g(n, number_of_coefficients, alpha)  # Summary classic_fit = lm(y ~ . + trt * ., data = df) av_fit = av(classic_fit, g = g_star) summary(av_fit) confint(av_fit)

title: Convert a Linear Model (lm) Object to Anytime-Valid lm (avlm) — av.lm
text: model lm object linear model fit. g positive precision parameter anytime-valid mixture (see Lindon et al., 2026, Section 4.3.1). acts like prior sample size: larger values favour smaller effects give narrower intervals large \(n\), cost wider intervals small \(n\). Use optimal_g choose target sample size. Default 1. vcov_estimator Optional character string specifying type heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors use. Must one "HC0", "HC1", "HC2", "HC3". NULL (default), robust variance estimation applied. combined cluster. cluster Optional cluster specification cluster-robust standard errors. Either vector cluster identifiers, one per observation used fitting model (e.g. respondent unit id); one-sided formula ~ cyl; single column name "cyl". Formulas column names evaluated data model fit , rows dropped fit (subset missing values) dropped clusters . one-way clustering supported. supplied, standard errors computed using CR1 cluster-robust sandwich estimator (scaled \(G/(G-1)\)), anytime-valid p-values confidence intervals use \(G - 1\) (clusters minus one) denominator degrees freedom, rather \(n - p\) (observations minus coefficients), number clusters \(G\) sample size, g cluster scale. cluster-robust e-values confidence sequences Lindon (2026). combined vcov_estimator. ... Additional arguments passed methods.

title: Coefficient Covariance and Degrees of Freedom for Anytime-Valid Inference — av_vcov
text:
Classical: \(s^2 (X'X)^{-1}\), \(
u = n - k\) (Lindon et al., 2026, Section 4). Heteroskedasticity-robust (HC0–HC3): sandwich \((X'X)^{-1} X'\Omega X (X'X)^{-1}\), \(
u = n - k\) (Lindon et al., 2026, Section 5). Cluster-robust (CR1): sandwich summed cluster scores scaled \(G/(G-1)\), \(
u = G - 1\) sample size \(G\) (Lindon, 2026, eq. CR1). Aliased (NA) coefficients dropped. weighted fits, rows \(X\) residuals scaled \(\sqrt{w}\) observations zero weight dropped.

text: anova() avlm object returns sequential ANOVA table anytime-valid p-values; previously silently returned classical table. warning given clusters coefficients, since cluster-robust covariance singular. confint() validates level; avaov summary prints g.

title: avlm 0.2.0
text: av.lm() gains cluster argument CR1 cluster-robust standard errors (sandwich scaled G / (G - 1), without Stata/fixest’s extra (n - 1) / (n - k)). cluster supplied, anytime-valid p-values, F-test, confidence intervals use G - 1 (clusters minus one) denominator degrees freedom, rather n - p (observations minus coefficients). cluster combined vcov_estimator. method described Lindon (2026), “Anytime-Valid Inference Linear Models Clustered Outcomes: Exact Multivariate Tests Cluster-Robust Confidence Sequences”, https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25613. cluster accepts vector cluster identifiers, one-sided formula (cluster = ~ cyl), column name (cluster = "cyl"). Formulas column names looked model’s data aligned observations used fit. cluster, anytime-valid sample size number clusters G, g cluster scale, joint F-test uses cluster-robust e-value exponent G/2. F-test p-value 1 cluster-robust covariance tested coefficients singular (e.g. fewer clusters tested coefficients). vcov() avlm object returns covariance used inference (classical, HC CR1). optimal_g() gains nu argument, can tune g cluster-robust inference (optimal_g(G, nu = G - 1, alpha = 0.05)). summary prints value g.

title: avlm 0.2.0
text: heteroskedasticity-robust (vcov_estimator) F-test now uses Wald statistic tested coefficients, inverting covariance rather taking block full precision matrix, stores Q / d. Previously evidence overstated testing one coefficient. confint() longer misplaces intervals fit aliased (NA) coefficients; previously every coefficient aliased one got NA wrong standard error. Heteroskedasticity- cluster-robust summaries fits longer fail singular-matrix error. Heteroskedasticity- cluster-robust standard errors now account weights (rows residuals scaled sqrt(w); zero weights dropped). Previously weights ignored, giving wrong standard errors weighted fits. Intercept-models now work vcov_estimator cluster. cluster now accepts one observation per cluster, gives HC0 sandwich scaled n / (n - 1). optimal_g() now searches g = 1, optimum lies small samples. Anytime-valid ANOVA p-values use number observations sample size; models without intercept one. av() checks g single positive number gives informative errors glm, multivariate (mlm) multi-stratum (Error()) fits instead failing later returning meaningless output.

title: avlm 0.2.0
